claims.text: The Stanford-published study of 5,172 customer-support agents reports an average15% increase in issues resolved per hour with AI assistance.
METR reports that16 experienced open-source developers completing246 tasks took19% longer with early-2025 AI tools in its randomized study.

editorial_building_blocks.1_reader: Managers and professionals responsible for approving work, with no cybersecurity or software-development expertise assumed.
editorial_building_blocks.2_decision: For one repeated task, compare the time to usable completion with and without AI, including checking and corrections; treat this as a proposed measurement, not a reported study result.
editorial_building_blocks.3_concept: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.

4_evidence.purpose: Support and bound the concept, rather than dictate a technical news summary.

beats: Begin with a familiar choice: is the work done when output appears, or when it can be used?
Compare the two attributed findings without pretending the settings are equivalent.
Explain the narrow measurement implication; distinguish proposed checking-and-correction measurement from a proven causal explanation.
End with the practical task comparison and a compact evidence boundary.

5_telling_voice.voice: relatable_provocateur v1; Graham Hill individual author
5_telling_voice.instruction: Explain ordinary decisions. Translate credentials as account access, whitelisted infrastructure as recognized company systems, API calls as direct computer-to-computer requests only if indispensable. No invented work experience, dialogue, screen-location assumptions or measured outcomes.

questions: Can a non-specialist paraphrase the point?
Is the telling useful beyond its opening?
